protocol.session: kernel-level micro: median of hundreds of sync'd reps per (context, variant) on gfx1151; fixed256-1024+gate chain vs qwen35_paged_full_attn_decode_split_k_gate_bf16_spans at splits 2/3/4
protocol.correctness: split-K output sanity-checked finite; not bit-exact vs the exact leaf (online-softmax) so not promoted
do_not_repeat: split-K (online-softmax + fused gate) for the c1 short-batch window <1024 (20-45% slower at 513-768, no reliable crossover)
WMMA-tile for the single-row c1 decode leaf (M=1 per block, latency-bound; 16x16 tiles waste 15/16 lanes)

mechanism_ab.conclusion: split-K is 20-45% slower at contexts 513-768; the splitK2 'win' at 1023 flips between runs (fixed 104-123 vs splitK2 101-109), within ~15-20% run variance at the top of the window. Not a reliable crossover; keep the fixed256-1024 leaf for <1024 and split-K for >=1024 (already routed).

reason: The c1 short-batch leaf is already at 1024 threads (the fastest measured block geometry) and the gate is negligible. split-K adds online-softmax merge overhead that loses to the leaf at the bulk of the c1 window; WMMA is structurally mismatched to the M=1, memory-latency-bound leaf. The c1 attention leaf is at its practical gfx1151 optimum; remaining full-attention headroom is the QKV/output projection family (separate owner).
